key_insight: Latent Drift forecasts slow neurodegenerative change by modeling progression in a compressed latent space instead of trying to regenerate full MRI anatomy.
clinical_relevance: If validated further, this approach could help anticipate future brain changes earlier, supporting more timely monitoring, trial planning, and treatment evaluation.
method: Learns progression in a semantic latent representation to reduce dominance of unchanged anatomy.
Uses Finite Scalar Quantization to filter out small nuisance fluctuations while keeping consistent structural drift.
Targets longitudinal MRI change directly, with progressive generative forecasting rather than full-image synthesis.
evidence_signal: On longitudinal 3D brain MRI, the method outperformed diffusion and autoregressive transformer baselines on both generative fidelity and clinically relevant metrics.
watch_item: Performance may depend on high-quality longitudinal MRI and careful validation to ensure latent forecasts reflect true disease drift rather than dataset-specific noise.
paper_title: Progression as Latent Drift: Generative Forecasting of Slow-Evolving Pathologies
